findings.title: TreeHash.tree_hash does not actually omit empty directories, contradicting its own docstring
locations: src/TreeHash.jl:38-39: "entries sorted by git's rule ... empty directories omitted."
findings.description: The docstring of `tree_hash` states "empty directories omitted" and that the function "reproduce[s] the object ids `git hash-object` and `git write-tree` would give". `_nonempty(path, skip)` returns a `Bool` (true/false), not a collection, and in Julia `isempty(::Bool)` is ALWAYS `false` (a scalar is a length-1 iterator) — verified: `julia -e 'println(isempty(true), " ", isempty(false))'` prints `false false`. So `isempty(_nonempty(path, skip)) && continue` NEVER triggers `continue`, and a genuinely empty subdirectory is always pushed into `entries` (as a `40000` tree entry hashing to git's well-known empty-tree id), never skipped. I verified this end-to-end: running the actual `tree_hash` body over a directory holding one empty subdirectory `emptysub` produced a root tree id of `7c334583827af7801cfd13c7d26236b81e34ce34` that INCLUDES an entry for `emptysub`, whereas real `git init && git add -A && git write-tree` on the identical directory gives `4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904` (git's canonical empty tree, since git tracks no empty directories at all). The function's actual behavior therefore directly contradicts both the "empty directories omitted" claim and the "reproduces what `git write-tree` would give" claim whenever the hashed tree contains any recursively-empty directory — a state that can occur in the tool's own consumer trees, e.g. `test/regressions/` right after `gbg init` but before `gbg sync` seeds its README, or an empty round scratch directory. Since `PIN.SELF`/`PIN.TREESHA`/`gbg self verify` and `TreeHash.tree_hash(dir)` in `Preflight.stamps` rely on this function matching git's own tree ids, this can produce a silently wrong tree hash rather than the documented one.
findings.resolution_hint: The intended check is "skip a directory that is empty", i.e. `_nonempty(path, skip) || continue` (skip when NOT nonempty), not `isempty(_nonempty(path, skip))`. Fix the condition, add a witness with a genuinely empty subdirectory compared against real `git write-tree`, and re-verify PIN.SELF/PIN.TREESHA against a tree containing one.

findings.title: Witnesses.run_one can classify a witness :blocked even though it also failed, contradicting "was never seen to fail"
locations: src/Witnesses.jl:32-33: ":blocked` (the file declares `# blocked: <reason>` and errored) ..." (WitnessResult docstring)
src/Witnesses.jl:145: "or `:blocked` (it errored, was never seen to fail, and carries a `# blocked: <reason>` header)"
src/Witnesses.jl:165-168: `if e > 0; blocked === nothing || return WitnessResult(name, :blocked, p, f, e, blocked); ... end`
findings.description: `run_one`'s docstring and `WitnessResult`'s docstring both state that `:blocked` means the witness "errored, was never seen to fail" — i.e. implying `fails == 0`. But the code's `if e > 0 ... blocked === nothing || return WitnessResult(name, :blocked, p, f, e, blocked)` branch returns `:blocked` purely from `e > 0` (an errored `@test`) and a present `# blocked:` header, without checking `f == 0`. I verified this by constructing a witness file with a `# blocked: …` header whose body contains both `@test 1 == 2` (a genuine failing assertion) and `@test error("boom")` (an errored assertion) in the same `@testset`; running the actual WRAPPER script that `run_one` uses produced `GBG_WITNESS pass=0 fail=1 error=1` — i.e. `f=1` and `e=1` simultaneously — which `run_one`'s logic classifies as `:blocked` (carrying the real fail count `f=1` in the `WitnessResult`, but reported to the operator only as BLOCKED with the header's reason, not as a failure). This means a witness that both encountered an unrelated error AND asserted a real, currently-true defect can be filed away as BLOCKED and never surfaces as the FAIL evidence `RULE.INST.WITNESS` requires, contradicting the documented "was never seen to fail" characterization of the BLOCKED state.
findings.resolution_hint: Require `f == 0` before returning `:blocked` in the `e > 0` branch (e.g. `f == 0 && blocked !== nothing && return WitnessResult(...,:blocked,...)`), so a witness that is also observed to fail is reported as `:fail`/`:broken` rather than silently absorbed into BLOCKED.
